sentences.text: 4. In course of hearing, Mr. Ajit Kumar Tripathy, learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that after the award has been passed under Section 3-G (1) and (2) of the National Highways Act, 1954 (for brevity "the Act"), the Petitioner filed an objection with regard to apportionment of the compensation.
The said application is still pending with the Competent Authority, Land Acquisition Officer (National Highway), Bhubaneswar.
He therefore submits that the objection filed by the Petitioner be referred to the Civil Court for taking a decision on the apportionment of the compensation.

5. Mr. Ajit Patnaik, learned counsel appearing for the National Highways Authority -Opposite Party Nos. 2 and 3 submits that due to pendency of W.P.(C) No. 13307 of 2017, no action has been taken by the Competent Authority.
The matter has been kept in abeyance on the request of the parties to the award.

6. In view of the submission made by learned counsel for the Parties, this Court feels that the Competent Authority - Land Acquisition Officer (National Highway), Bhubaneswar without keeping the matter pending with itself, should have referred it to the Civil Court for adjudication of the reference.

sentences.text: 7. Accordingly, it is directed that the objection filed by the Petitioner shall be referred to the Civil Court for proper adjudication in view of Section 3-H(4) of the Act.
8. The Writ Petition is accordingly disposed of.
9. The case record of W.P.(C) No. 13304 of 2017 be detached and send back to the concerned section immediately for taking steps to list the matter before the assigned Bench.
(K.R. Mohapatra) Judge (Savitri Ratho) Judge Sukanta Signed by: SUKANTA KUMAR BEHERA
